title: Spatio-Temporal Provenance Guard: Detecting Privilege Escalation Attacks That Exploit Spatio-Temporal Data Loss in Multi-Agent MCP Environments
content: Multi-agent systems built on the MCP (Model Context Protocol) let agents of different trust and privilege share records across sessions. The provenance of a record, its source, writer, trust, and privilege, is normally dropped at storage and session boundaries, a loss we call spatio-temporal data loss. This opens a privilege-escalation path: an adversary controlling only an ingestion path can spread an outbound-transfer directive over individually incomplete records that a high-privilege agent later assembles and executes. We propose STPG (Spatio-Temporal Provenance Guard), a gateway defense that persists connector provenance on write, reassembles records by lineage on read, and authorizes privileged routing calls only when a trusted directive is witnessed to target the actual destination and verified against a deterministic support path. On a Google Cloud testbed with Gemini agents, STPG blocked every assembled attack and passed every approved external transfer, whereas a conservative provenance gate blocked all approved transfers and an attribution judge misattributed a fifth of them; it also matched every specified decision on a policy challenge set. Robustness tests locate its limits: literal binding blocks approved calls whose identifier is written differently, and a swapped judge model keeps the gate decisions but lowers detection, while multi-connector attacks remain blocked.
